transcript:
00:00:00 Ethan: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — Ethan from Redwood, with Lina and Maya on the call. how's everyone doing?
00:00:05 Daniel: good, thanks. excited to see the tracing stuff, we've had a couple of incidents where latency spiked and we couldn't quickly find root cause.
00:00:14 Lina: awesome, that's exactly what we'll walk through — console tracing, request logs, debug flows. we'll demo a couple of real DEBUG traces and show how to track an error from SDK to model runtime. warning: transcript auto-generated so some names might be off.
00:00:30 Priya: quick logistics — we care about PII redaction, KMS, and whether logs leave our VPC.
00:00:38 Maya: totally, we'll cover redaction and the private deployment options. short answer: hosted has redaction controls + opt-in KMS; Dedicated/Private gives you customer-managed KMS and no egress from your VPC.
00:00:55 Ethan: ok jumping into the console — top left is the tracing tab, you can filter by time, model, route, and trace-id. i'll click an example trace where a request took 1.2s at token 10 then spiked to 3.5s.
00:01:12 Ethan: you'll see trace spans — api gateway, routing, model-inference, kv-cache lookup. here we have a cache miss at the KV lookup span and a long compile/quantize kernel selection span.
00:01:30 Tom: is that the kernel selection that sometimes happens on cold-start?
00:01:33 Lina: yep, that compile span is typically 100-300ms on first warmup, we show it in trace so you can correlate spikes. you can annotate a span with a rollout policy or model variant tag.
00:01:51 Daniel: how do we correlate this to our request ids? our app uses a request_id header.
00:01:56 Maya: good question — we support passing through x-request-id and we surface it in the trace metadata. you can search traces by that header value or export trace-id back to your logs.
00:02:12 Priya: and payloads — full input text, are those stored?
00:02:17 Ethan: by default we persist request logs with redaction for PII; you can toggle full payload capture in Dedicated/Private with customer consent and KMS encryption. in hosted, we store hashed inputs for matching and redact detected PII, and we have retention controls.
00:02:38 Laura: retention length?
00:02:40 Lina: default 30 days for full request logs, 90 days for aggregated metrics — can be extended as an add-on. in Private you control retention fully.
00:02:52 Ethan: i'll open a trace with an error span — see the error: "decode_failed" at model-output stage, model returned malformed json. the request log shows the prompt and the model version 1.2.3-quant.
00:03:06 Ethan: you can click to open the request log — shows headers, prompt, tokenization stats, kv cache hit/miss and per-token timing. note the tokenization shows extra tokens due to a control char in the prompt.
00:03:22 Daniel: could that be from our frontend sanitizer?
00:03:25 Tom: we had that a while back, yeah.
00:03:27 Lina: exactly — the trace helps you see the chain: request enters, our router picks a variant, checks KV cache, then calls the runtime. we surface model variant, quantization profile, and whether fallback happened.
00:03:40 Ethan: here's an example where routing fallback to a cheaper model is automatic when latency SLO is missed — the trace shows two inference spans with different model names and a final aggregator span.
00:03:55 Priya: so in the trace we'd see both?
00:03:58 Maya: yes, both spans and the reason code — "fallback: latency_slo" — so you can see if fallbacks caused lower quality.
00:04:07 Daniel: that helps, we want to audit when fallback happened and if that caused customer-visible regressions.
00:04:12 Ethan: next i'll show request logs search — you can query by status code, model, route, latency buckets, and custom header.
00:04:22 Ethan: typing a query now for status:500 and model:1.2.3* in the last 24 hours. results show three traces — i'll open the most recent.
00:04:35 Ethan: notice in the request log we surface stack traces from our runtime when available, and an inferred probable cause (e.g., JSON parse error, OOM).
00:04:45 Laura: Runtime stack traces — are those sanitized? could they include our PII?
00:04:50 Lina: we redact user content by default and you can enable additional redaction rules. stack traces themselves are runtime-level; we can suppress them at the cluster/tenant level for Private deployments.
00:05:02 Tom: about sampling — we don't want every request logged at full fidelity, costs blow up. how does sampling work?
00:05:09 Ethan: good — we support adaptive sampling: error traces are 100%, slow traces 100%, and normal traffic sampled at a rate you configure (e.g., 1 in 100). we also give suggestions based on your target storage cost.
00:05:23 Priya: where do the sampled logs live? is it in our region?
00:05:26 Maya: hosted stores traces in the region you select; Dedicated offers tenant-local storage; Private stores everything in your infra. we also support cross-region replication if you want longer term analytics in a central region.
00:05:39 Daniel: and encryption at rest?
00:05:41 Ethan: AES-256 by default, and for customer-managed keys we integrate with KMS/HSMs — we documented the exact flow in the security pack we'll send.
00:05:51 Priya: ok thanks.
00:05:55 Lina: moving on to error analysis — console has automated histograms by error type, you can click an error bucket to jump to representative traces and the top contributing prompts.
00:06:08 Ethan: i'll show an example: malformed-json errors spiked after a model rollout — console highlights the rollout and shows which prompts interact badly with the new quant profile.
00:06:20 Ethan: you can run a quick eval against a sample prompt set and we show pass/fail per model variant. this is integrated with Redwood Optimize suggestions.
00:06:30 Daniel: that integration — can we automate rollback if eval fails?
00:06:33 Maia: (slight name mismatch) Lina: we have canary policies — you can configure automated rollback on error rate or latency regressions. full automation requires a Dedicated plan for safety controls.
00:06:50 Priya: curious about how request logs tie to billing — do logs count toward token billing?
00:06:55 Ethan: logs and metrics are billed separately; token billing is for inference. logs storage and retention is charged by GB-month and ingestion. we can include estimated costs in the benchmark sheet.
00:07:08 Tom: in the trace you mentioned KV cache hits — can we see cache hit ratio over time?
00:07:12 Lina: yes we have a cache dashboard and per-route stats; trace spans include cache.hit=true/false and latency of lookup. you can filter traces by cache miss to correlate cost spikes.
00:07:25 Daniel: we're also running some orchestration that does batching; will batching appear in traces?
00:07:30 Maya: batching appears as a batch-inference span with batch-size metadata. you'll see per-token timings and an aggregation span. it also shows when a request waited in the queue for batching.
00:07:44 Priya: excellent.
00:07:47 Ethan: quick demo of request log export — you can bulk export traces to S3 or to your SIEM (we have a connector for Splunk/Datadog). export supports anonymization rules on the fly.
00:08:02 Laura: Splunk connector — is it push or pull?
00:08:05 Lina: we push via secure HTTPS with mutual TLS; in Dedicated we can also mount an S3 bucket in your account.
00:08:13 Daniel: if we do a POC, what's the recommended retention for capturing enough data but keeping costs down?
00:08:19 Ethan: for POC we recommend 7-14 day full capture with adaptive sampling for normal traffic; that usually gives enough error cases and a decent latency baseline.
00:08:29 Tom: we need to run a burst test with 200 QPS — will tracing add measurable overhead?
00:08:35 Lina: tracing adds small overhead on ingest path, typically 2-5% CPU on control plane; it shouldn't affect inference latency significantly. for high-QPS we recommend sampling down non-error traces and using aggregated metrics for baseline.
00:08:49 Daniel: can we instrument our instrumentation to inject our internal trace id?
00:08:52 Maya: yes we accept x-request-id and x-trace-parent headers; we also support OpenTelemetry exporters in Private.
00:09:02 Priya: about RBAC — can we restrict who sees PII?
00:09:05 Ethan: yes, RBAC at role level; you can restrict access to full payloads to specific roles and audit access in the console.
00:09:14 Laura: we need to see the audit log format, please include that in the security packet.
00:09:18 Ethan: will do.
00:09:21 Lina: quick note on debugging flows — when you drill into a trace you can open a side-by-side diff between two traces to see token-by-token differences and timing deltas. it's helpful for model regressions.
00:09:36 Ethan: here's an example diff between stable and rollout — you can see tokenization diverged early.
00:09:44 Daniel: could we get an alert that points to the representative trace?
00:09:47 Maya: yes alerts can embed a trace link and include the top 5 example traces in the alert payload.
00:09:56 Priya: what about telemetry retention for compliance, like longer-term audit?
00:09:59 Lina: we offer extended retention as an add-on or via Private where you control storage. export to your S3 for immutable archives is common.
00:10:10 Ethan: moving toward Q&A — anything else from the security side?
00:10:15 Laura: SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning?
00:10:18 Ethan: supported; SAML SSO and SCIM for user sync; we'll include configuration docs.
00:10:25 Daniel: ok this has been helpful. quick recap demo checklist then next steps —
00:10:31 Ethan: recap: tracing shows spans (api, routing, kv, inference), you can search by headers or request-id, sample aggressively for cost control, automated error buckets + eval integration, and export to SIEM.
00:10:44 Ethan: next steps: we'll send SOC2, KMS integration notes, sample benchmark, and propose POC dates.
00:10:52 Priya: timeline — can we do the POC next week Wed/Thu?
00:10:56 Ethan: Lina, Maya available Thu. we'll set up an hour-long POC with a demo tenant.
00:11:02 Lina: noted. i'm going to paste some console links in the follow-up notes.
00:11:06 Daniel: thanks everyone.
00:11:08 Ethan: thank you, bye.
00:11:10 (call ends)
